translation_notes: helpers.py: load_prefixes/_bind_prefixes_to_graph/resolve_uri/ensure_declaration/reconstruct_intersection are the real module-level helpers copied verbatim from kracr/cog-csv-owl-bridge@d238191ecc's src/csv_to_owl/csv_owl_code.py (they sit above the extracted region in the same file, so the draft's original.py could not run without them). Fixture data (subclass.csv, prefixes.csv) exercises all five branches of the function: simple A<=B, textual 'some' restriction, '&' intersection, an on-property/quantifier restriction column, and the empty-Subclass GCI row.

driver.py bypasses run_pair's entry=/calls= mechanism: the function's whole observable effect is the OWL file it serializes (no graph argument, no return value), so comparing only its string arguments would be a hollow green. The driver instead calls each side's function directly and compares the two serialized files by rdflib graph isomorphism, using the same harness helpers run_pair itself uses.
blank nodes (restriction, anon_cls) stay plain BNode() -- the original never keys them on data, so there is nothing for _:{ } to hash; not listed as a construction used.

Credit correction (2026-11-02, corpus/403 defect 3): dropped `@prefix` for `rdf:`, `xsd:`, declared by the mechanical draft but never used as a term in the translated region (and not among the bindings the original sets on its graph); `rdfeval check` stays OK.

repair.driver: Four cases instead of one, each also comparing return value, stdout (WARN lines decide the branch; output path masked), whether a file is written, and the xmlns declarations of the written RDF/XML (original's set must be in the translation's): 'synthetic' (the former CSV, unchanged); 'branches' (A <= all R.C, quantifier 'only' and 'SOME', textual 'all' restriction, textual restriction without superclass, intersection without superclass, row without quantifier, property-only row, GCI with 'some'); 'repo' (the repository's own subclass.csv and prefixiri.csv, copied verbatim as subclass_repo.csv and prefixiri_repo.csv: default ':' prefix on the OWL namespace, xml:base, other column order); 'missing' (nonexistent CSV: no file written). Temporary directory now removed.
mutants_killed: owl:allValuesFrom island of the A <= R.C case removed
allValuesFrom -> someValuesFrom in the A <= R.C case
simple A <= B subClassOf island removed
owl namespace rebound to another prefix before serialisation
repair.remaining: Not a repair flag: the translator's note says helpers.py is copied verbatim, but _bind_prefixes_to_graph lost its comments and its `return bound_count` (no effect here, the caller ignores it); the note stays inaccurate.

credit_correction.what: unused prefix declarations dropped from translated.ldpy

optimization_notes: optimized.py: the A ⊑ (∃R.C)/(∀R.C) branch reuses build_restriction instead of re-writing its four adds, and is merged with the GCI branch (same guard on property, quantifier and superclass; `if subclass_str` decides the subClassOf direction); build_restriction picks someValuesFrom/allValuesFrom by a conditional expression; find_col becomes one `next(...)` generator; the `(x or "")` guards go (values are str after fillna("")); the `... if x_str else None` guards and the `parts`/`len(parts) > 1` logic go (resolve_uri already returns None silently for an empty string; str.partition replaces split); the intersection's two list comprehensions become one; the trailing `continue`s of the last branches become an `elif` chain. Every try/except, return and printed WARN survives in the same order.

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: `g = Graph()` becomes `@graph as g`; build_restriction's three adds become one `+{ {b} a owl:Restriction ; owl:onProperty … ; {owl:someValuesFrom if … else owl:allValuesFrom} … }` (shared subject, island only; the predicate chosen by a Python conditional over prefixed names in an interpolation hole); the other adds become `+{ }`; OWL.Class/OWL.ObjectProperty arguments become owl:Class/owl:ObjectProperty.
Blank nodes stay BNode(): build_restriction returns its node and anon_cls is the subject of a conditional triple, so no `[ ]` can absorb them.
Symmetry: outside the RDF lines the two files are identical line for line.
The driver now emits its verdict through harness._emit, which credits the sides it executed: rdfeval check proves every artefact.
header_optimization_notes: Python: URIRef, Literal, XSD, Namespace and the duplicate Graph go; the three rdflib imports merge into `from rdflib import Graph, BNode, RDF, RDFS, OWL`; pandas and the helpers import stay.
LD Python: every rdflib name but BNode goes (`@graph as g`, owl:, rdfs: replace them); both @prefix lines are used.
